expectations.evidence: All figures survive (41 to 19 min p95, 12% to 87% in two weeks, 3 of 11 services at 70%, 6 minutes from sharding, $2,400/month, Priya's quote), and "the cache and the test shards did the rest" only restates what the original implies.
No em dashes, staged reveals or cliches; "The result?" and "Let's dive in" are gone, and the close is a plain recap ("Builds went from 41 minutes to 19.") rather than an uplifting sign-off.
Wording is concrete and sentence lengths vary, e.g. "Most of our time wasn't spent compiling. It was spent downloading the same dependencies over and over again."
It stays a plain engineering team blog post with headings, a code block and the refrain, neither hype nor a bullet list.
